stem: The brainstem comprises which of the following:
fact: The brainstem comprises the midbrain, pons, and medulla.
finding: NCBI brainstem anatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: The blood supply to the temporal lobe is primarily supplied by which of the following arteries:
fact: The temporal lobe receives lateral supply from the MCA and medial supply from the PCA.
mnemonic: Temporal lobe: MCA lateral, PCA medial.
finding: NCBI cerebral blood-supply anatomy supports the displayed combination.

stem: The basilar artery is formed from which of the following blood vessels:
fact: The two vertebral arteries unite at the pontomedullary junction to form the basilar artery.
mnemonic: Vertebrals converge to make the basilar.

stem: A 29 year old male racing driver has fractured a cervical vertebra. On examination, he has weakness of the right side of his body with upgoing plantars, loss of pain and temperature sensation in his left limbs, with normal fine-touch sensation over all four limbs. This clinical picture is most likely seen in a lesion of the:
fact: A right lateral spinal-cord lesion affects the ipsilateral corticospinal tract and contralateral spinothalamic pathway while sparing dorsal-column fine touch.
finding: NCBI Brown-Séquard anatomy supports right lateral-column localization.

stem: A 65 year old man has resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia and a shuffling gait. Parkinson's disease results from which of the following mechanisms:
options: A vascular lesion of the subthalamic nucleus
Loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra
Loss of serotonergic neurons in the globus pallidus and red nucleus
Defect in the metabolism of copper
Loss of cholinergic and GABAergic neurons in the caudate nucleus and putamen
fact: Parkinson disease involves degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra with striatal dopamine depletion.
finding: Source explanation and standard neuroanatomy support the displayed key.

stem: Which of the following best describes the function of the cerebral aqueduct:
options: Major site of production of CSF
Connects the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle
Drains CSF into the subarachnoid cisterns
Connects the third ventricle to the fourth ventricle
Connects the right and left lateral ventricles
fact: The cerebral aqueduct connects the third ventricle to the fourth ventricle.
finding: Standard ventricular anatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: What type of visual field defect would you most likely see in a lesion of the optic radiation of the left temporal lobe:
fact: The left temporal optic radiations carry lower fibres representing the right superior visual quadrant, so injury causes right homonymous superior quadrantanopia.
mnemonic: Temporal Meyer loop: contralateral upper quadrant.

stem: What type of visual field defect are you most likely to see in a lesion of the optic nerve:
fact: An optic-nerve lesion causes ipsilateral monocular visual loss before the chiasm.
mnemonic: Optic nerve before crossing: one eye.
finding: NCBI visual-pathway anatomy supports monocular loss.

stem: Which of the following clinical features is most suggestive of a lesion of the occipital lobe:
fact: Occipital-lobe lesions commonly produce homonymous visual-field loss.
mnemonic: Occipital cortex is the visual cortex.

stem: The blood supply to the occipital lobe is primarily supplied from which of the following arteries:
fact: The occipital lobe is primarily supplied by the posterior cerebral artery, with additional MCA supply possible at the occipital poles.
mnemonic: PCA powers the posterior visual cortex.
finding: NCBI PCA anatomy supports the displayed key and source caveat.
